ledger.claim: The driver's own trace never passes the CTE (Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 towards City) gantry that the fare ledger charges $6.00 for: the nearest fix is 1,159.02 m from the gantry, far outside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09(4) applies, the trace does not bracket the gantry's closest approach (gap_brackets_closest_approach is false) and the line is carried as crossed:false. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure: it is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists, and it must be recorded as a billing-integrity finding. That is precisely the rider's complaint — 'he never took the expressway — no gantry' — and the telemetry proves it.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip (fare_breakdown.fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 75.00), so POL-RD-02 does not run and the distance and time lines were fixed at booking; the rider's remedy is POL-RD-11(a), the amount by which charged_total (81.00) exceeds the quoted fare (75.00) plus the pass-through lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. No pass-through line is properly chargeable here — the only ERP line was never crossed, there is no airport surcharge on a non-airport trip and waiting_time_fee is 0.00 — so 81.00 - 75.00 = 6.00 is refundable. That is the same figure the ledger's own pol_rd_11_remedy field computes (6.00). The ledger records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the rider is still carrying the disputed charge.

On the distance question the trace governs, not the receipt: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 31.49 km against an optimal 28.00 km, an excess of 3.49 km or 12.46%, which fails the 20% and 0.8 km POL-RD-01 establishment tests. The rider does not overreach on that point and seeks no distance-or-time refund — on an upfront-quoted trip none is available. What the trace does establish is the rider's real complaint: the vehicle never went near the expressway whose gantry it was billed to cross.

The driver cannot claim exoneration under POL-RD-04 for any part of the route: the in-app chat export for this trip is empty (message_count 0, no messages, first_message_at null). POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log, corroborated by chat_message.waypoint_hint or a named road; with no chat content there is no instruction and no waypoint_hint, the corroboration test cannot be run on the record, and the clause is unavailable.

The driver's explanation — 'local roads were faster that day' — asserts an external traffic cause for the extra distance. Under POL-RD-13 that assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, and there is no such advisory: EV-ADVIS-00532-01 is disclosed here as MISSING, carries weight_multiplier 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and has no payload (it is cited for its absence only), so no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window. POL-RD-03 is therefore unavailable, the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and it supplies neither a reduction of the excess nor an amended optimal route.

The driver's own statement admits a second passenger — 'the other passenger was a short hop, no delay' — yet the trip_record records vehicle_type RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL. POL-RD-12's exclusion for collecting or setting down a co-rider applies only to a platform-matched pooled itinerary (RYDE_POOL); it cannot be used to explain distance on this solo booking. The admission also corroborates the rider's account that another passenger was carried on a ride booked and paid for as a solo trip, which bears on how much weight the driver's assertions about the fare line are given.

The rider's route-deviation claim fails at the first gate. The governing distance is the GPS polyline, gps_trace.trace_distance_km 31.49 km — trip_record.actual_distance_km 31.5 km is the rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may NOT be cited for the threshold test — measured against the booked optimal of 28.0 km. That is an excess of 3.49 km, or 12.46% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be BOTH greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms; 12.46% fails the percentage limb decisively, so no deviation is established and, on the clause's own words, the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The excess is not merely below the establishment gate, it is nowhere near material. 3.49 km is far under the 8.0 km absolute materiality figure and 12.46% is far under the 50% figure, so the deviation is neither established nor material and POL-RD-06's repeat-pattern enquiry is never engaged on this trip.

Even if that enquiry were engaged, no repeat-deviation pattern is available against this driver: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 250, short of both the three-flag test and the 0.05 ratio test, so none of POL-RD-06's three effects can follow. The clause is explicit that a pattern may never be used to establish that this particular trip deviated — that finding must rest on this trip's trace alone, and this trip's trace is under the threshold.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and limb (b) requires an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. This trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 289 fixes at a 10-second cadence over the 48-minute trip, 100% coverage, no gaps recorded, and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 s, so none of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is met. Limb (b) therefore fails, the burden never shifts, and the driver is never required to point to any exculpatory artifact at all.

This trip is priced UPFRONT_QUOTE: quoted_fare_sgd is 75.00 and fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE. Under POL-RD-11 POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess, because the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and the rider was already whole on those lines. On this fare model the ordinary consequence of a detour is a cost borne by the driver, not a refund to the rider — the rider cannot recover the upside of a risk the pricing model never placed on him.

The rider's appeal to other riders who 'got a full refund for less', and the request for the whole 81.00, has no clause behind it. POL-RD-11 limits the remedy on an upfront-quoted trip to the arithmetic difference between charged_total and quoted_fare_sgd plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. There is no parity entitlement between cases and no discretionary round-number payment anywhere in this policy; the figure is fixed by the clause, not by comparison with strangers.

The rider's premise that 'the platform refunded half' is not in the record at all: the fare ledger records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so no refund has been issued on this trip and nothing has been reversed. NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03 is party-relative — it leaves payment_status and refund_issued_sgd exactly as they stand — and on a rider-filed dispute over a charge that still stands, that means the charge stands.

The rider's second complaint — that the driver 'picked someone else up when I paid for a solo ride' — is not a ground of refund under this policy. The booking is a RYDE_X trip, and POL-RD-12, the only clause that addresses distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider, applies where trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_POOL; it is not RYDE_POOL here. The chat log for this trip holds 0 messages and no artifact in the bundle records a second pickup, so an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight under POL-RD-08. In any event the fare was fixed at booking, so any extra time on the road did not change what the rider paid (POL-RD-11).

Even on the rider's best case the money is small and capped. The rider paid charged_total 81.00 against a quoted_fare_sgd of 75.00, and the entire 6.00 difference is a single ERP line. POL-RD-11(a) refunds only the excess of charged_total over the quoted fare plus pass-through lines 'actually crossed' under POL-RD-09; the platform's own comparison puts the trace's closest approach to that gantry at 1,159 m, well outside the POL-RD-09(4) crossing radius, so that 6.00 can only travel as a pass-through correction. The driver does not resist that 6.00 — it is government-set ERP, never driver revenue — but it is the ceiling: the remaining 75.00 of the rider's claim is the quoted fare he agreed to, and it fails on POL-RD-01, POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-11.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The fare on this trip was fixed at booking as an upfront quote of SGD 75.00, and the total charged was SGD 81.00 — the SGD 6.00 difference being a single ERP line for the CTE (Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 towards City) gantry.

Distance. The GPS polyline governs (POL-RD-01). The trip record's 31.5 km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement; the governing trace_distance_km is 31.49 km against a booked optimal of 28.00 km — an excess of 3.49 km, or 12.46%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of optimal and 0.8 km absolute; 12.46% fails the percentage limb, so no deviation is established and no distance refund arises. On an UPFRONT_QUOTE fare POL-RD-11 independently closes that route: POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available however large the excess, because those lines were fixed at booking and the rider was already whole on them.

The ERP line — this is where money moves. The platform's own comparison puts the trace's closest fix 1,159.02 m from the gantry, far outside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09(4) applies, and the trace does not bracket the closest approach (gap_brackets_closest_approach false; the line is carried crossed:false). The gantry was therefore never crossed. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge line for a gantry the trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. SGD 6.00 is refunded. POL-RD-11(a) yields the same figure on its own arithmetic — charged_total 81.00 less quoted_fare 75.00 less properly chargeable pass-through lines 0.00 = 6.00 — and the two are not added together (POL-RD-11(b) is not stacked on (a)). Rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, the refund is SGD 6.00.

Driver's traffic explanation. 'Local roads were faster that day' asserts an external traffic cause. POL-RD-13 tests that against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. EV-ADVIS-00532-01 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, no payload), so no advisory covers this window, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver cited no advisory identifier, this is an uncited assertion and not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact: it is a gap in the bundle, not the POL-RD-10(5) contradiction, so no escalation follows. The assertion neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal route.

Second-passenger complaint. The booking is a RYDE_X solo trip; POL-RD-12's co-rider exclusion applies only to a platform-matched RYDE_POOL itinerary, so it does not apply here and cannot explain distance on this booking. The chat log holds 0 messages and no artifact records a second pickup, and the fare was fixed at booking, so this complaint produces no refund under this policy. The driver's statement does admit a second passenger was carried; that admission is noted, but no clause of this policy grounds a monetary remedy in it.

Repeat-pattern check. POL-RD-06 is not engaged: there is no material deviation, and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 with completed_trips_90d 250, so no pattern exists and no driver-conduct referral arises.

Parity. The rider's comparison with other refunds, and the request for the whole SGD 81.00, have no clause behind them; this policy fixes the figure by the clause arithmetic, not by comparison. The rider's belief that the platform already refunded half is not borne out by the record — payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00.

Confidence. The deciding facts — that the trace never crossed the gantry, and the charged total against the quoted fare — rest on EV-GPS-00532 and EV-FARE-00532, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and is not moved by the MISSING advisory at weight 0.0, which carries no fact and is cited only for its absence.

Amount. Of the contested SGD 81.00, SGD 6.00 is refunded; the remaining SGD 75.00 is the quoted fare agreed at booking and stands.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 6.00 CTE (Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 towards City) ERP line was charged for a gantry the GPS trace never passed (nearest fix 1,159.02 m, outside the 250 m crossing radius) and has been refunded in full as a standalone pass-through correction.
